title: A Village Tide Calendar
paras: For many years, people in a small fishing village kept a tide calendar. It began in 1954, when a boat builder named Tomas bought a notebook with part of his [[salary|salary]]. Each evening, he watched the [[moon|moon]] and wrote down when the sea reached the harbour steps. He wanted to understand the [[difference|difference]] between high water on different days. Before this, village families had kept [[such|such]] information in their heads.

Tomas also wrote a story inside the cover. It was about a [[king|king]] who showed that even a ruler could not stop the sea. Tomas read it to his daughter, Lina, in a deep [[voice|voice]]. They often played a guessing game: whose tide time would be closer to the real time? At twelve, Lina finally [[beat|beat]] her father. She had carefully studied his old notes.

In 1976, Lina bought a small [[calculator|calculator]]. It helped her work with the numbers more quickly. By then, many village boats used [[petrol|petrol]], but their owners still needed enough water to leave the harbour safely. Lina made paper calendars for them. She [[hope|hoped]] her work would make their journeys easier. Today, the first notebook sits in the village museum, open beside one of her calendars.
zh: 多年来，一个小渔村的人们一直记录着潮汐日历。这件事始于1954年，当时一位名叫托马斯的造船工拿出一部分薪水，买了一本笔记本。每天傍晚，他观察月亮，并记下海水涨到港口台阶的时间。他想弄清楚，不同日子的涨潮有什么差异。在此之前，村里的家庭都是把这类信息记在脑子里的。
托马斯还在封面内侧写了一个故事。故事讲的是一位国王，他让人们看到，即使是统治者也无法阻止海水上涨。托马斯用低沉的嗓音把故事读给女儿莉娜听。他们经常玩猜时间的游戏：谁猜的涨潮时间更接近实际时间？十二岁时，莉娜终于赢了父亲。她曾仔细研究过他以前的记录。
1976年，莉娜买了一台小计算器，帮助她更快地处理数字。那时，村里许多船已经使用汽油，但船主们仍然需要等水位足够高，才能安全驶出港口。莉娜为他们制作纸质潮汐日历。她希望自己的工作能让他们的出行更轻松。如今，最初的那本笔记本陈列在村庄博物馆里，摊开放在她制作的一张日历旁边。

q.s: Tomas used some money from his job to buy his first notebook.
q.why: 他用部分薪水买了笔记本。

q.s: Lina first won the tide guessing game when she was ten.
q.why: 文中说她十二岁时才赢了父亲。

q.s: Lina sold her paper calendars to boat owners.
q.why: 只说她为船主制作日历，未提收费。
